selected_problem: Fresh-main inspection found NorthStarRunner marked a validation as READY_FOR_DELIVERY solely from command/browser acceptance. A validation command could mutate a path belonging to the applied changesets, exit successfully, and leave delivery eligible even though the protected postimage no longer matched the applied transaction receipt and rollback could become conflicted.

decision_provenance.mode_route_basis: Fresh-main inspection isolated one evidence-rich central validation/delivery integrity gap in the existing engineering loop. The committed four-mode router's singular-bottleneck gate routes the replay to DEEP_DEVELOPMENT; no forced rotation was used.
decision_provenance.claim_limit: No hosted DWAC success receipt or fabricated numeric DWAC score is claimed.

pre_fix_reproduction.source_observation: NorthStarRunner.validate used runAcceptance(...).passed directly to choose READY_FOR_DELIVERY versus REPAIR_REQUIRED, without re-checking the applied changeset paths after validation execution.
pre_fix_reproduction.consequence: A successful validator that rewrites a protected path could make unreceipted bytes or metadata eligible for delivery and invalidate rollback optimistic-concurrency assumptions.

changes: Added a bounded validation postimage snapshot over the union of paths recorded by the run's changesets, capturing existence, type, content SHA-256, object identity, and regular-file mode.
After command/browser acceptance, the same protected paths are re-observed; any drift is recorded and an otherwise passing validation is converted to VALIDATION_POSTIMAGE_DRIFT / REPAIR_REQUIRED.
Validation evidence now carries the postimage-integrity receipt so delivery eligibility is traceable to both behavioral acceptance and unchanged applied code reality.
The postimage comparison and gating rule are isolated in a small directly tested helper; unchanged paths pass, content mutation fails, and mode-only mutation fails on POSIX.

validation.tests: 3/3 focused validation-integrity regressions PASS; 0 skipped on the Linux verification host

truth_boundaries: This protects paths represented by the run's applied changesets from validator-induced drift becoming deliverable; it does not sandbox validation or prohibit side effects on unrelated workspace paths, external files, processes, or the network.

Detected drift is failed closed and recorded; this patch does not automatically restore validator side effects, because silently mutating the workspace during validation cleanup would require a separate sovereignty and recovery design.
OS-level validation sandboxing, arbitrary complex semantic synthesis, Windows descendant-tree equivalence, and crash-level filesystem atomicity remain unresolved.
No GitHub Actions are intentionally triggered or rerun, no force push is used, and no credential, payment, formal Release, or destructive/irreversible external action is performed.
